lines: Now the glad-hearted should wend to the worship-ground —
where the heart grows glad, fit for the Lord's embrace,
that alone the mark, and naught besides;
for e'en as told, the thought one with the thought is cause,
and that from gladness alone — no other ground.
tsa-a13-v01.sanskrit_cite: atha prasannahṛdayo yāgasthānaṃ yāyāt tac ca yatraiva hṛdayaṃ prasādayuktaṃ parameśvarasamāveśayogyaṃ bhavati tad eva na tu asya anyal lakṣaṇam uktāv api dhyeyatādātmyam eva kāraṇam tad api bhāvaprasādād eva iti nānyat sthānam

lines: But seat and summit and the rest in writ are known
as pointing to this ground alone.
tsa-a13-v02.sanskrit_cite: pīṭhaparvatāgram ityādis tu śāstre sthānoddeśa etatpara eva boddhavyaḥ

lines: In these seats and the rest, by the Highest's decree,
powers, by the Highest entered, take on flesh —
as Aryan lands for the righteous,
as outcast lands for the unrighteous;
the mountain-top word, through lonely calm
shunning stray thoughts, is one-pointedness' seat.
tsa-a13-v03.sanskrit_cite: teṣu teṣu pīṭhādisthāneṣu parameśaniyatyā parameśvarāviṣṭānāṃ śaktīnāṃ dehagrahaṇāt āryadeśā iva dhārmikāṇāṃ mlecchadeśā iva adhārmikāṇām parvatāgrādeś caikāntatvena vikṣepaparihārāt aikāgryapadatvam iti

lines: There before the worship-house, without, alone,
the common rite be done — first on hands, then on frame.
tsa-a13-v04.sanskrit_cite: tatra yāgagṛhāgre bahir eva sāmānyanyāsaṃ kuryāt karayoḥ pūrvaṃ tato dehe

lines: hrīṃ na pha hrīṃ, hrīṃ ā kṣa hrīṃ — thus;
by these twain, voicing Might and Might's lord,
the Mālinī-alphabet twin spells;
with each alone: first Might, then the Mighty —
in release from foot-tip to crown's end;
in revelry all turned about.
tsa-a13-v05.sanskrit_cite: hrīṃ na pha hrīṃ hrīṃ ā kṣa hrīṃ ity ābhyāṃ śaktiśaktimadvācakābhyāṃ mālinīśabdarāśimantrābhyām ekenaiva ādau śaktiḥ tataḥ śaktimān iti muktau pādāgrāc chiro'ntam bhuktau tu sarvo viparyayaḥ

lines: For goddess Mālinī is Might's chief mien,
all cravings milking through seed-and-womb's clash.
tsa-a13-v06.sanskrit_cite: mālinī hi bhagavatī mukhyam śāktaṃ rūpaṃ bījayonisaṃghaṭṭena samastakāmadugham

lines: And meet is this her name: garlanded with Rudra's strings of might,
in fruits abloom, the hum that ends the winter of the world,
holding winning and release,
with gift-and-grasping might endued —
since ra and la are one, 'tis said.
tsa-a13-v07.sanskrit_cite: anvarthaṃ caitan nāma rudraśaktimālābhir yuktā phaleṣu puṣpitā saṃsāraśiśirasaṃhāranādabhramarī siddhimokṣadhāriṇī dānādānaśaktiyuktā iti ralayor ekatvasmṛteḥ

lines: Hence e'en a broken rite is whole by this rite's power;
and e'en a tainted Garuḍa-Vaiṣṇavite
becomes, stainless grown, release-bestowing.
tsa-a13-v08.sanskrit_cite: ata eva hi bhraṣṭavidhir api mantra etannyāsāt pūrṇo bhavati sāñjano 'pi gāruḍavaiṣṇavādir nirañjanatām etya mokṣaprado bhavati

lines: From body's rite, the same rite decks the bowl.
For here, that ever-unswerving belief
we are one with our Lord be firmed by rite —
for example this; how the doer's ground,
the upbuilding of the purified seat, the cleansing
of the wine-cup's vessel, and, built on this,
the body's, the god's altar by abode.
tsa-a13-v10.sanskrit_cite: iha hi kriyākārakāṇāṃ parameśvarābhedapratipattidārḍhyasiddhaye pūjākriyā udāharaṇīkṛtā tatra ca sarvakārakāṇām itthaṃ parameśvarībhāvaḥ tatra yaṣṭrādhārasya sthānaśuddhyāpādānakaraṇayor arghapātraśuddhinyāsābhyām yaṣṭur dehanyāsāt yājyasya sthaṇḍilādinyāsāt

lines: Thus by mere rite the doer, made all of the Lord,
holds all doings with this very gaze,
sans chiefest ken and yogin sway —
becomes the Highest Lord.
tsa-a13-v11.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ kriyākrameṇāpi parameśvarīkṛtasamastakārakaḥ tayaiva dṛśā sarvakriyāḥ paśyan vināpi pramukhajñānayogābhyāṃ parameśvara eva bhavati

lines: From the bowl so decked, with bloom and incense blest,
its drops sprinkle forth the rite's pith with the bloom of power.
tsa-a13-v12.sanskrit_cite: evam arghapātre nyasya puṣpadhūpādyaiḥ pūjayitvā tadvipruḍbhir yāgasāraṃ puṣpādi ca prokṣayet

lines: Then in bright orb, on earth, in sky, or forth:
'oṃ to the outer train' — hail — thus do worship.
tsa-a13-v13.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ prabhāmaṇḍale bhūmau khe vā oṃ bāhyaparivārāya nama iti pūjayet

lines: Then at the doorway station:
'oṃ to the portal's god-ring' — hail — thus do worship.
tsa-a13-v14.sanskrit_cite: tato dvārasthāne oṃ dvāradevatācakrāya nama iti pūjayet

lines: But where a guardless wold without doth lie,
enter thou, and on the altar's edge alone
the outward-host, the portal-god-ring worship do,
as shown before, and rite, yet nothing without.
tsa-a13-v15.sanskrit_cite: agupte tu bahiḥsthāne sati praviśya maṇḍalasthaṇḍilāgra eva bāhyaparivāradvāradevatācakrapūjāṃ pūrvoktaṃ ca nyāsādi kuryāt na bahiḥ

lines: Then, chanting thrice phaṭ, swoosh —
by arms enspelled, cast thou the flower,
blot the blocks, low falling, brood within,
with radiance-laden look of the Highest kindled,
gaze round about the worship-house.
tsa-a13-v16.sanskrit_cite: tato 'pi phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ iti astrajaptapuṣpaṃ prakṣipya vighnān apasāritān dhyātvā antaḥ praviśya parameśvarakiraṇeddhayā dṛṣṭyā abhito yāgagṛhaṃ paśyet

lines: There liberation's lover, northward facing, stand,
that by the Lord's fell-fire splendour, swift indeed,
his bands burnt off, he free remain.
tsa-a13-v17.sanskrit_cite: tatra mumukṣur uttarābhimukhas tiṣṭhet yathā bhagavadaghoratejasā jhaṭity eva pruṣṭapāśo bhavet

lines: There the Lord's free will alone, by a mien's show,
the compass-principle shines forth.
tsa-a13-v18.sanskrit_cite: tatra parameśvarasvātantryam eva mūrtyābhāsanayā diktattvam avabhāsayati

lines: There mind-light alone is the middle; thence other shapes spring:
to be held as light is above, what is not so is below;
what looks to light is east, the other west;
from mutual light turned, the next is that high-course stream-raising station;
south out of favour, facing it, but from to-be-shown, north —
thus the fourfold compass-cross.
tsa-a13-v19.sanskrit_cite: tatra citprakāśa eva madhyaṃ tata itarapravibhāgapravṛtteḥ prakāśasvīkāryam ūrdhvam atathābhūtam adhaḥ prakāśanasammukhīnaṃ pūrvam itarat aparam saṃmukhībhūtaprakāśatvāt anantaraṃ tatprakāśadhārārohasthānaṃ dakṣiṇam ānukūlyāt tatsammukhaṃ tu avabhāsyatvāt uttaram iti dikcatuṣkam

lines: There in the midst the Lord; above, his is the north-eastern face;
below, the underworld face; in the east-and-rest four directions, the so-called Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Sadyas, Vāma; in the four-direction-middle, the other four.
tsa-a13-v20.sanskrit_cite: tatra madhye bhagavān ūrdhve 'sya aiśānaṃ vaktram adhaḥ pātālavaktram pūrvādidikcatuṣke śrītatpuruṣāghorasadyovāmākhyaṃ dikcatuṣkamadhye anyāś catasraḥ

lines: Thus awareness-bliss alone, plain wrought,
shows difference of the compass — thus compass is no other thing.
tsa-a13-v21.sanskrit_cite: ity evaṃ saṃvinmahimaiva mūrtikṛtaṃ digbhedaṃ bhāsayati iti dik na tattvāntaram

lines: As, as the shade is to o'erleap — being, before, before, it stands —
so to the Highest's mid-point arrival: being o'er all is middle-hood — so said.
tsa-a13-v22.sanskrit_cite: yathā yathā ca svacchāyā laṅghayitum iṣṭā satī puraḥ puro bhavati tathā parameśvaramadhyatām eti sarvādhiṣṭhātṛtaiva mādhyasthyam ity uktam

lines: As the Lord parts the quarters, so the sun —
for his is the Highest's knowing might, so sung:
there, there, there the east is, where the manifest
was east before; and just where, so there —
thus self-ruled, yet facing one's own ground, stands first.
tsa-a13-v23.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ yathā bhagavān digvibhāgakārī tathā sūryo 'pi sa hi pārameśvary eva jñānaśaktir ity uktaṃ tatra tatra tatra pūrvaṃ vyakteḥ pūrvā yatraiva ca tathā tatraiva evaṃ svātmādhīnāpi svasammukhīnasya deśasya purastāttvāt

lines: Thus by self, sun, Lord — the triad made one —
is the compass mused: so Abhinava's masters.
Thus standing, face north and sit, burn body-hood
in frame, breath, city-eight and the rest, by I-sense cast off;
then, near, as in another's frame, from disembodiedness —
through mounting the waveless, steadfast abode,
whose nature is gaze — which indeed is the first throb-digit —
that alone is form; thereon, as taught,
the worship-to-be god-wheel plant;
chiefly here to be worshipped are the Powers.
tsa-a13-v25.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ sthite uttarābhimukham upaviśya dehapuryaṣṭakādau ahambhāvatyāgena dehatāṃ dahet saṃnidhāv api paradehavat adehatvāt tato nistaraṅgadhruvadhāmarūḍhasya dṛṣṭisvābhāvyāt yā kila ādyā spandakalā saiva mūrtiḥ tadupari yathopadiṣṭayājyadevatācakranyāsaḥ prādhānyena ca iha śaktayo yājyāḥ

lines: From being that seat, of the Lord-nine-fold self and the rest,
of power alone, for worship-worthiness —
so say the masters.
tsa-a13-v26.sanskrit_cite: tadāsanatvāt bhagavannavātmādīnāṃ śakter eva ca pūjyatvāt iti guravaḥ

lines: There the five states, waking first;
and sixth, the Unsurpassed by name,
the inborn station — ever to be dwelt upon.
tsa-a13-v27.sanskrit_cite: tatra ca pañca avasthā jāgradādyāḥ ṣaṣṭhī ca anuttarā nāma svabhāvadaśā anusaṃdheyā

lines: Thus sixfold is the placing done.
There, by the seat of causes — Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Rulers, gracious Sadāśiva —
severally, from the six-and-thirty-count nature-transcending bounds,
in Bhairava-Lord-non-difference course,
the placing, from fullness, is Bhairavī-being —
hence this has no opening.
tsa-a13-v29.sanskrit_cite: tatra kāraṇānāṃ brahmaviṣṇurudreśasadāśivaśaktirūpāṇāṃ pratyekam adhiṣṭhānāt ṣaṭtriṃśattattvakalāpasya laukikatattvottīrṇasya bhairavabhaṭṭārakābhedavṛtte nyāse pūrṇatvāt bhairavībhāvaḥ tena etat anavakāśam

lines: Which, they cry: gained in waveless mounting,
what again with nature-forthbringing,
by placing and the rest — thus.
tsa-a13-v30.sanskrit_cite: yad āhuḥ ataraṅgarūḍhau labdhāyāṃ punaḥ kiṃ tattvasṛṣṭir nyāsādinā iti

lines: So far indeed that waveless Bhairava-formed,
which in own self shows forth-dissolve-variety's utmost.
tsa-a13-v31.sanskrit_cite: tāvat hi tad ataraṅgaṃ bhairavavapuḥ yat svātmani avabhāsitasṛṣṭisaṃhārāvaicitryakoṭi

lines: Thus by mutual-meeting-yoga, Lord-made breath-body-mind
contemplated, without, within,
with blossoms, smoke, sating and the rest, as may be — worship.
tsa-a13-v32.sanskrit_cite: evam anyonyamelakayogena parameśvarībhūtaṃ prāṇadehabuddhyādi bhāvayitvā bahir antaḥ puṣpadhūpatarpaṇādyair yathāsambhavaṃ pūjayet

lines: There in frame, breath, mind moist, the thorned lotus for worship bring —
as at the root of power-substance: seed, bulb, pith to the root's sap,
in the hanging-end, to the kalā-principle's end the staff;
the Māyā-natured knot; the four-natured pure-lore lotus;
right there the ever-blest Sadāśiva — he alone the great corpse —
through excellence dissolved, from waking, chief:
from knowable-bodied body-decay, and from sound-touch-knowing —
thus.
tsa-a13-v33.sanskrit_cite: tatra śarīre prāṇe dhiyi ca tadanusāreṇa śūlābjanyāsaṃ kuryāt tad yathā ādhāraśaktimūle mūlaṃ kanda āmūlasārakaṃ lambikānte kalātattvānto daṇḍaḥ māyātmako granthiḥ catuṣkikātmā śuddhavidyāpadmaṃ tatraiva sadāśivabhaṭṭārakaḥ sa eva mahāpretaḥ prakarṣeṇa līnatvāt bodhāt prādhānyena vedyātmakadehakṣayāt nādāmarśātmakatvāc ca iti

lines: That risen from the navel, venting through the triple crown-gate above,
dwelling within sound, a spreading power,
of even mind and form and the rest, the six-end;
thereon the pure tri-lotus, past the mind;
on this world-made division, made a seat,
presiding in pervading guise,
the wished-for, upheld being,
the goddess to be shaped —
which here, in self-sameness-full nature,
world-being-offered: that alone is worship;
which, the same, becoming-that: that is brooding;
which by such inward musing's steadfast poise: that is murmur;
which by such musing's order-wakened splendour's might:
by that force alone is all-world-selfing:
that is the burnt-gift;
that done, the train, from That
as sparks from a fire-heap,
musing thus, worship just so.
tsa-a13-v34.sanskrit_cite: tan nābhyutthitaṃ tanmūrdharandhratrayanirgataṃ nādāntarvartiśaktivyāpinīsamanārūpamarātrayaṃ dviṣaṭkāntaṃ tadupari śuddhapadmatrayam aunmanasam etasmin viśvamaye bhede āsanīkṛte adhiṣṭhātṛtayā vyāpakabhāvena ādheyabhūtāṃ yathābhimatāṃ devatāṃ kalpayitvā yat tatraiva samasvabhāvanirbharātmani viśvabhāvārpaṇaṃ tad eva pūjanaṃ yad eva tanmayībhavanaṃ tad dhyānaṃ yat tathāvidhāntaḥparāmarśasadbhāvanādāndolanaṃ sa japaḥ yat tathāvidhaparāmarśakramaprabuddhamahātejasā tathābalād eva viśvātmīkaraṇaṃ sa homaḥ tad evaṃ kṛtvā parivāraṃ tata eva vahnirāśer visphuliṅgavat dhyātvā tathaiva pūjayet

lines: Twelve's-end, this foremost, thorn-set —
mind, from the root, with pith replete.
tsa-a13-v35.sanskrit_cite: dvādaśāntam idaṃ prāgraṃ viśūlaṃ mūlataḥ smaran

lines: Leaving sequence, goddess-wheel-front-going
attains sky-faring-ness.
From root's base, twice-six-end-sky-crown-filling-natured.
Of sky-faring-ness, from sky-roving-rest and from sky-nectar-feasting.
Thus by inward rite alone, in sooth, is done what was to do.
Truly for the then-entered, still outer is to be done, to cut off the bound —
and who too thus shares not the sinking —
his chief is the outer rite;
from its doing, sinking's gain;
since for him too, but the beast-veiling inner rite,
when mounted thereon, of his thought-force is purity-giving.
tsa-a13-v40.sanskrit_cite: satyataḥ tadāviṣṭasya tathāpi bahir api kāryo yāgo 'vacchedahānaya eva yo 'pi tathā samāveśabhāk na bhavati tasya mukhyo bahiryāgaḥ tadabhyāsāt samāveśalābho yatas tasyāpi tu paśutātirodhānāyāntaryāgaḥ tadarūḍhāv api tatsaṃkalpabalasya śuddhipradatvāt

lines: Now, when initiation one fain would do — then for staying's sake:
ground-taking, Gaṇeśa-worship, jar-and-jug worship,
altar-worship, oblation — thus do.
tsa-a13-v41.sanskrit_cite: atha yadā dīkṣāṃ cikīrṣet tadādhivāsanārthaṃ bhūmiparigrahaṃ gaṇeśārcanaṃ kumbhakalaśayoḥ pūjāṃ sthaṇḍilārcanaṃ havanaṃ ca kuryāt

lines: But in daily-and-seasonal: altar-and-the-rest worship-oblation alone.
There is the staying, the pupil's cultured fitness-placing —
as the whetting of teeth; the God's toward-work-upturned-ness-grasping,
the master's taking of that.
tsa-a13-v43.sanskrit_cite: tatra adhivāsanaṃ śiṣyasya saṃskṛtayogyatādhānam amblīkaraṇam iva dantānāṃ devasya kartavyonmukhatvagrāhaṇam guros tadgrahaṇam

lines: Of rite-things, indoors abiding in the worship-house,
through the Lord's out-blooming glory,
bestowing worship-gear's fitness — thus.
There, the worship-house with all gear replete arranged,
having brought to mind the blest Mālinī or Mother,
full of her-letter-splendour's mass, bearing the taken,
musing, the flower-handful cast.
tsa-a13-v45.sanskrit_cite: tatra sarvopakaraṇapūrṇaṃ yāgagṛhaṃ vidhāya bhagavatīṃ mālinīṃ mātṛkāṃ vā smṛtvā tadvarṇatejaḥpuñjabharitaṃ gṛhītaṃ bhāvayan puṣpāñjaliṃ kṣipet

lines: Then the said weapon-muttered white grain and the rest, splendour-formed,
having strewn, in the north-east quarter gather in order —
thus the ground-taking.
tsa-a13-v46.sanskrit_cite: tata uktāstrajaptāni yathāsambhavaṃ siddhārthadhānyākṣatalājādīni tejorūpāṇi vikīrya aiśānyāṃ diśi krameṇa saṃghaṭṭayet iti bhūparigrahaḥ

lines: Then, the seat to pure-lore's term given, Gaṇeśa worshipped;
then the jar, with bliss-stuff filled, adorned, worshipped;
then the to-be-worshipped next, the betel placed,
there the chief spell, all-presiding, remembering, with rule before —
with that, a hundred-and-eight-muttered, that jar be made.
tsa-a13-v47.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ śuddhavidyāntam āsanaṃ dattvā gaṇapateḥ pūjā tataḥ kumbham ānandadravyapūritam alaṃkṛtaṃ pūjayet tato yājyam anu pūgaṃ nyasya tatra mukhyaṃ mantraṃ sarvādhiṣṭhātṛtayā vidhipūrvakatvena smaran aṣṭottaraśatamantritaṃ tena taṃ kumbhaṃ kuryāt

lines: In the twin jar, for stumbling-quelling, the weapon worship.
Then in own quarters the world-wards with weapons worship.
Then to the fore-hallowed pupil's hand the weapon-jar give.
tsa-a13-v50.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ śiṣyasya prāk dīkṣitasya haste astrakalaśaṃ dadyāt

lines: And himself the master the jar take up.
Then the pupil pouring the stream round the house for stumbling-quelling,
with jar let him follow, this spell reciting:
ho, ho! Indra! by thee in thine own quarter, for stumbling-pacifying.
tsa-a13-v52.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ śiṣyaṃ gṛhaparyanteṣu vighnaśamanāya dhārāṃ pātayantaṃ sakumbho 'nugacchet imaṃ mantraṃ paṭhan bho bhoḥ śakra tvayā svasyāṃ diśi vighnapraśāntaye

lines: With heedfulness, to rite's end must it be, by Śiva's behest.
In the three-syllabled name, 'ho' is one alone — thus.
tsa-a13-v54.sanskrit_cite: tryakṣare nāmni bho ity ekam eva

lines: Then in the north-east quarter the jar establish.
Upon the strewn, the weapon-jar.
Then worship of the twain.
Then in the altar's midst the Highest's worship.
Then the fire-pit as Highest-Might-formed mused, the fire kindled there,
with heart-inward waking-fire made one,
with spell-musing's train, the blazing Śiva-fire mused,
there placed, worshipped, the spells with ghee and grain to sate.
tsa-a13-v59.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ agnikuṇḍaṃ parameśvaraśaktirūpatayā bhāvayitvā tatra agniṃ prajvālya hṛdayāntarbodhāgninā saha ekīkṛtya mantraparāmarśasāhityena jvalantaṃ śivāgniṃ bhāvayitvā tatra nyasya abhyarcya mantrān tarpayet ājyena tilaiś ca

lines: And with the bowl, the sprinkling alone is grain-and-ghee's refining.
tsa-a13-v60.sanskrit_cite: arghapātreṇa ca prokṣaṇam eva tilājyādīnāṃ saṃskāraḥ

lines: And of ladle-and-spoon, no-difference-view alone indeed is refining.
tsa-a13-v61.sanskrit_cite: sruksruvayoś ca parameśābhedadṛṣṭir eva hi saṃskāraḥ

lines: Then offered as may be, the ladle-spoon up-down-faced, as might-and-Śiva formed,
mutually facing, arranged, even-footed risen,
musing the stream of supreme nectar fallen, risen in the sky of the twelve-end, risen full-Śiva-moon,
and breathing the vauṣaḍ-ending spell, till ghee's end stand —
thus the full-pouring, spell-wheel-sating.
tsa-a13-v62.sanskrit_cite: tato yathāśakti hutvā sruksruvau ūrdhvādhomukhatayā śaktiśivarūpau parasparonmukhau vidhāya samapādotthito dvādaśāntagaganoditaśivapūrṇacandraniḥsṛtapatatparāmṛtadhārābhāvanāṃ kurvan vauṣaḍantaṃ mantram uccārayan ca ājyakṣayāntaṃ tiṣṭhet iti pūrṇāhutiḥ mantracakrasaṃtarpaṇī

lines: Then the sprinkled grain brought, on hearth-vessel-jar-fires share by share offered,
one share left over, to the pupil a share give.
tsa-a13-v63.sanskrit_cite: tataś caruṃ prokṣitam ānīya sthaṇḍilakalaśakumbhavahniṣu bhāgaṃ bhāgaṃ nivedya ekabhāgam avaśeṣya śiṣyāya bhāgaṃ dadyāt

lines: Then the tooth-twig.
Its fall in fire, Death's, No-Light's quarters, below, is ill — thus.
tsa-a13-v65.sanskrit_cite: tatpāto 'gniyamanirṛtidikṣu adhaś ca na śubha iti

lines: There by weapon-spell the burnt-gift be done.
Then the stumbling shunned, to see the coming spell made worthy,
bring the blindfold pupil in, make him kneel,
cast thou the blossom-handful.
tsa-a13-v67.sanskrit_cite: tato vikṣepaparihāreṇa bhāvimantradarśanayogyatāyai baddhanetraṃ śiṣyaṃ praveśya jānusthitaṃ taṃ kṛtvā puṣpāñjaliṃ kṣepayet

lines: Then swift, eye-cloth loosed of him — through grace-descent blessed means —
seeing face to face the present spell of that station, made of that he becomes;
of graced means the spell-presence is plain,
since as if trembling, the beings.
tsa-a13-v68.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ sahasā apāsitanetrabandho 'sau śaktipātānugṛhītakaraṇatvāt saṃnihitamantraṃ tatsthānaṃ sākṣātkāreṇa paśyan tanmayo bhavati anugṛhītakaraṇānāṃ mantrasaṃnidhiḥ pratyakṣaḥ yatas trasyatām iva bhūtānām

lines: Then in one's own right hand, blazing, the god-wheel worshipped,
that hand burning the pupil's bonds on crown-heart-navel, lay down.
tsa-a13-v69.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ svadakṣiṇahaste dīpyatayā devatācakraṃ pūjayitvā taṃ hastaṃ mūrdhahṛnnābhiṣu śiṣyasya pāśān dahantaṃ nikṣipet

lines: Then in the left with gentleness, worshipped, fattened with pure truth —
then make obeisance.
tsa-a13-v70.sanskrit_cite: tato vāme somyatayā pūjayitvā śuddhatattvāpyāyinaṃ tataḥ praṇāmaṃ kuryāt

lines: Then the being-god-quarter-bali, with wine-flesh-ghee full,
without bestow — sip thou.
tsa-a13-v71.sanskrit_cite: tato bhūtadevatādigbaliṃ madyamāṃsajalādipūrṇaṃ bahir dadyāt ācāmeta

lines: Then, thyself the grain-feast done, with pupil-self oneness won,
awakened-natured, stay.
tsa-a13-v72.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ svayaṃ carubhojanaṃ kṛtvā śiṣyātmanā saha aikyam āpannaḥ prabuddhavṛttiḥ tiṣṭhet

lines: Dreaming too, at dawn if the pupil an ill dream tell,
that to him expound thou not.
tsa-a13-v73.sanskrit_cite: svapan api prabhāte śiṣyaḥ cet aśubhaṃ svapnaṃ vadet tat asmai na vyākuryāt

lines: For doubt-and-fear would his be; with weapon alone its cleansing do.
tsa-a13-v74.sanskrit_cite: śaṅkātaṅkau hi tathāsya syātām kevalam astreṇa tanniṣkṛtiṃ kuryāt

lines: Then just so the Highest worshipped, into him by the pupil's breath-course entered,
touching the six-fold six in heart-throat-palate-brow-cleft-twelve's-end,
each eight refinings musing, somewhile the pupil's breath there resting,
again descend.
tsa-a13-v75.sanskrit_cite: tatas tathaiva parameśvaraṃ pūjayitvā tadagre śiṣyasya prāṇakrameṇa praviśya hṛtkaṇṭhatālulalāṭarandhradvādaśānteṣu ṣaṭsu kāraṇaṣaṭkasparśaṃ kurvan pratyekam aṣṭau saṃskārān cintayan kaṃcit kālaṃ śiṣyaprāṇaṃ tatraiva viśramayya punar avarohet

lines: Thus effected-eight-and-forty refinings, made Rudra's part:
a time-bound one becomes.
Then to him the worship-to-be spell with blossoms and the rest bestow.
tsa-a13-v77.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ asmai pūjyaṃ mantraṃ puṣpādyaiḥ saha arpayet

lines: Then the vows to him set forth.
In master whole-souled, love; so in writ; in God; from their foes aversion;
as to the master, to master's son and the rest;
of lore-bound wrought, of fore-hallowed and the rest, beholding;
of womb-tie, for its honouring, not of self — thus deem.
tsa-a13-v79.sanskrit_cite: gurau sarvātmanā bhaktiḥ tathā śāstre deve tatpratidvaṃdvini parāṅmukhatā guruvat guruputrādeḥ vidyāsambandhakṛtasya tatpūrvadīkṣitādeḥ saṃdarśanam yaunasambandhasya tadārādhanārtham na tu svata iti mantavyam

lines: Woman's — of the barren a loathing-cause make thou not.
God-name, master-name, and spell, save at worship's hour, breathe thou not.
tsa-a13-v81.sanskrit_cite: devatānāma gurunāma tathā mantraṃ pūjākālāt ṛte na uccārayet

lines: What the master has enjoyed — couch and the rest — enjoy thou not.
What games and the rest are worldly, that, the master by, do thou not.
tsa-a13-v83.sanskrit_cite: yat kiṃcit laukikaṃ krīḍādi tat gurusaṃnidhau na kuryāt

lines: Save by that, elsewhere excellence-fancy make thou not.
Everywhere, at sire-rites and the rest, the master alone worship.
And in all occasionals, she-goblin and the rest — utter no names.
tsa-a13-v86.sanskrit_cite: sarveṣu ca naimittikeṣu śākinītyādiśabdān na vadet

lines: Feast-days worship keep.
With the down-looking Vaiṣṇavas and the rest, company keep thou not.
tsa-a13-v88.sanskrit_cite: vaiṣṇavādyair adhodṛṣṭibhiḥ saha saṃgatiṃ na kuryāt

lines: Abiding in this writ, with former-birth conceit, regard thou not.
When the master's circle to thy house has come, as thou canst, worship do.
The downward-pathed, though Vaiṣṇavite and the rest,
having e'en made him thy master, from his writ-clan cast away.
tsa-a13-v91.sanskrit_cite: adhomārgasthitaṃ kaṃcit vaiṣṇavādyaṃ tacchāstrakulāt gurūkṛtyāpi tyajet

lines: Even then with excellence-fancy regard him not.
With lingam-bearers make no mingling rite;
them only as thou canst, worship.
tsa-a13-v93.sanskrit_cite: liṅgibhiḥ saha samācāramelanaṃ na kuryāt tān kevalaṃ yathāśakti pūjayet

lines: Doubts abandon thou.
In the wheel abiding, last-and-first sundering, birth-wrought, fancy thou not.
tsa-a13-v95.sanskrit_cite: cakre sthitaś caramāgryādivibhāgaṃ janmakṛtaṃ na saṃkalpayet

lines: Apart from frame, no other seat or ford and the rest with high honour regard.
tsa-a13-v96.sanskrit_cite: śarīrāt ṛte na anyat āyatanatīrthādikaṃ bahumānena paśyet

lines: Mantra-heart unceasing mind thou — thus the pupil, hearing, bowing,
owning, to the master, with fee to wife-and-wealth-and-frame,
well-pleasing, sating fore-hallowed and needy-fatherless.
tsa-a13-v97.sanskrit_cite: mantrahṛdayam anavarataṃ smaret ity evaṃ śiṣyaḥ śrutvā praṇamya abhyupagamya guruṃ dhanadāraśarīraparyantayā dakṣiṇayā paritoṣya pūrvadīkṣitāṃś ca dīnānāthādikān tarpayet

lines: And by the future rule the image-wheel sate thou.
So is the timeling made.
In spell-practice, daily worship, hearing, study — entitled;
but in the occasional, everywhere, the master alone beseech.
tsa-a13-v100.sanskrit_cite: mantrābhyāse nityapūjāyāṃ śravaṇe 'dhyayane adhikārī naimittike tu sarvatra gurum eva abhyarthayet

lines: Thus is the timeling's rule.
Now the glad-hearted should wend to the worship-ground —
where the heart grows glad, fit for the Lord's embrace,
that alone the mark, and naught besides;
for e'en as told, the thought one with the thought is cause,
and that from gladness alone — no other ground.
tsa-a13-v01.sanskrit_cite: atha prasannahṛdayo yāgasthānaṃ yāyāt tac ca yatraiva hṛdayaṃ prasādayuktaṃ parameśvarasamāveśayogyaṃ bhavati tad eva na tu asya anyal lakṣaṇam uktāv api dhyeyatādātmyam eva kāraṇam tad api bhāvaprasādād eva iti nānyat sthānam

lines: But seat and summit and the rest in writ are known
as pointing to this ground alone.
tsa-a13-v02.sanskrit_cite: pīṭhaparvatāgram ityādis tu śāstre sthānoddeśa etatpara eva boddhavyaḥ

lines: In these seats and the rest, by the Highest's decree,
powers, by the Highest entered, take on flesh —
as Aryan lands for the righteous,
as outcast lands for the unrighteous;
the mountain-top word, through lonely calm
shunning stray thoughts, is one-pointedness' seat.
tsa-a13-v03.sanskrit_cite: teṣu teṣu pīṭhādisthāneṣu parameśaniyatyā parameśvarāviṣṭānāṃ śaktīnāṃ dehagrahaṇāt āryadeśā iva dhārmikāṇāṃ mlecchadeśā iva adhārmikāṇām parvatāgrādeś caikāntatvena vikṣepaparihārāt aikāgryapadatvam iti

lines: There before the worship-house, without, alone,
the common rite be done — first on hands, then on frame.
tsa-a13-v04.sanskrit_cite: tatra yāgagṛhāgre bahir eva sāmānyanyāsaṃ kuryāt karayoḥ pūrvaṃ tato dehe

lines: hrīṃ na pha hrīṃ, hrīṃ ā kṣa hrīṃ — thus;
by these twain, voicing Might and Might's lord,
the Mālinī-alphabet twin spells;
with each alone: first Might, then the Mighty —
in release from foot-tip to crown's end;
in revelry all turned about.
tsa-a13-v05.sanskrit_cite: hrīṃ na pha hrīṃ hrīṃ ā kṣa hrīṃ ity ābhyāṃ śaktiśaktimadvācakābhyāṃ mālinīśabdarāśimantrābhyām ekenaiva ādau śaktiḥ tataḥ śaktimān iti muktau pādāgrāc chiro'ntam bhuktau tu sarvo viparyayaḥ

lines: For goddess Mālinī is Might's chief mien,
all cravings milking through seed-and-womb's clash.
tsa-a13-v06.sanskrit_cite: mālinī hi bhagavatī mukhyam śāktaṃ rūpaṃ bījayonisaṃghaṭṭena samastakāmadugham

lines: And meet is this her name: garlanded with Rudra's strings of might,
in fruits abloom, the hum that ends the winter of the world,
holding winning and release,
with gift-and-grasping might endued —
since ra and la are one, 'tis said.
tsa-a13-v07.sanskrit_cite: anvarthaṃ caitan nāma rudraśaktimālābhir yuktā phaleṣu puṣpitā saṃsāraśiśirasaṃhāranādabhramarī siddhimokṣadhāriṇī dānādānaśaktiyuktā iti ralayor ekatvasmṛteḥ

lines: Hence e'en a broken rite is whole by this rite's power;
and e'en a tainted Garuḍa-Vaiṣṇavite
becomes, stainless grown, release-bestowing.
tsa-a13-v08.sanskrit_cite: ata eva hi bhraṣṭavidhir api mantra etannyāsāt pūrṇo bhavati sāñjano 'pi gāruḍavaiṣṇavādir nirañjanatām etya mokṣaprado bhavati

lines: From body's rite, the same rite decks the bowl.
For here, that ever-unswerving belief
we are one with our Lord be firmed by rite —
for example this; how the doer's ground,
the upbuilding of the purified seat, the cleansing
of the wine-cup's vessel, and, built on this,
the body's, the god's altar by abode.
tsa-a13-v10.sanskrit_cite: iha hi kriyākārakāṇāṃ parameśvarābhedapratipattidārḍhyasiddhaye pūjākriyā udāharaṇīkṛtā tatra ca sarvakārakāṇām itthaṃ parameśvarībhāvaḥ tatra yaṣṭrādhārasya sthānaśuddhyāpādānakaraṇayor arghapātraśuddhinyāsābhyām yaṣṭur dehanyāsāt yājyasya sthaṇḍilādinyāsāt

lines: Thus by mere rite the doer, made all of the Lord,
holds all doings with this very gaze,
sans chiefest ken and yogin sway —
becomes the Highest Lord.
tsa-a13-v11.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ kriyākrameṇāpi parameśvarīkṛtasamastakārakaḥ tayaiva dṛśā sarvakriyāḥ paśyan vināpi pramukhajñānayogābhyāṃ parameśvara eva bhavati

lines: From the bowl so decked, with bloom and incense blest,
its drops sprinkle forth the rite's pith with the bloom of power.
tsa-a13-v12.sanskrit_cite: evam arghapātre nyasya puṣpadhūpādyaiḥ pūjayitvā tadvipruḍbhir yāgasāraṃ puṣpādi ca prokṣayet

lines: Then in bright orb, on earth, in sky, or forth:
'oṃ to the outer train' — hail — thus do worship.
tsa-a13-v13.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ prabhāmaṇḍale bhūmau khe vā oṃ bāhyaparivārāya nama iti pūjayet

lines: Then at the doorway station:
'oṃ to the portal's god-ring' — hail — thus do worship.
tsa-a13-v14.sanskrit_cite: tato dvārasthāne oṃ dvāradevatācakrāya nama iti pūjayet

lines: But where a guardless wold without doth lie,
enter thou, and on the altar's edge alone
the outward-host, the portal-god-ring worship do,
as shown before, and rite, yet nothing without.
tsa-a13-v15.sanskrit_cite: agupte tu bahiḥsthāne sati praviśya maṇḍalasthaṇḍilāgra eva bāhyaparivāradvāradevatācakrapūjāṃ pūrvoktaṃ ca nyāsādi kuryāt na bahiḥ

lines: Then, chanting thrice phaṭ, swoosh —
by arms enspelled, cast thou the flower,
blot the blocks, low falling, brood within,
with radiance-laden look of the Highest kindled,
gaze round about the worship-house.
tsa-a13-v16.sanskrit_cite: tato 'pi phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ iti astrajaptapuṣpaṃ prakṣipya vighnān apasāritān dhyātvā antaḥ praviśya parameśvarakiraṇeddhayā dṛṣṭyā abhito yāgagṛhaṃ paśyet

lines: There liberation's lover, northward facing, stand,
that by the Lord's fell-fire splendour, swift indeed,
his bands burnt off, he free remain.
tsa-a13-v17.sanskrit_cite: tatra mumukṣur uttarābhimukhas tiṣṭhet yathā bhagavadaghoratejasā jhaṭity eva pruṣṭapāśo bhavet

lines: There the Lord's free will alone, by a mien's show,
the compass-principle shines forth.
tsa-a13-v18.sanskrit_cite: tatra parameśvarasvātantryam eva mūrtyābhāsanayā diktattvam avabhāsayati

lines: There mind-light alone is the middle; thence other shapes spring:
to be held as light is above, what is not so is below;
what looks to light is east, the other west;
from mutual light turned, the next is that high-course stream-raising station;
south out of favour, facing it, but from to-be-shown, north —
thus the fourfold compass-cross.
tsa-a13-v19.sanskrit_cite: tatra citprakāśa eva madhyaṃ tata itarapravibhāgapravṛtteḥ prakāśasvīkāryam ūrdhvam atathābhūtam adhaḥ prakāśanasammukhīnaṃ pūrvam itarat aparam saṃmukhībhūtaprakāśatvāt anantaraṃ tatprakāśadhārārohasthānaṃ dakṣiṇam ānukūlyāt tatsammukhaṃ tu avabhāsyatvāt uttaram iti dikcatuṣkam

lines: There in the midst the Lord; above, his is the north-eastern face;
below, the underworld face; in the east-and-rest four directions, the so-called Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Sadyas, Vāma; in the four-direction-middle, the other four.
tsa-a13-v20.sanskrit_cite: tatra madhye bhagavān ūrdhve 'sya aiśānaṃ vaktram adhaḥ pātālavaktram pūrvādidikcatuṣke śrītatpuruṣāghorasadyovāmākhyaṃ dikcatuṣkamadhye anyāś catasraḥ

lines: Thus awareness-bliss alone, plain wrought,
shows difference of the compass — thus compass is no other thing.
tsa-a13-v21.sanskrit_cite: ity evaṃ saṃvinmahimaiva mūrtikṛtaṃ digbhedaṃ bhāsayati iti dik na tattvāntaram

lines: As, as the shade is to o'erleap — being, before, before, it stands —
so to the Highest's mid-point arrival: being o'er all is middle-hood — so said.
tsa-a13-v22.sanskrit_cite: yathā yathā ca svacchāyā laṅghayitum iṣṭā satī puraḥ puro bhavati tathā parameśvaramadhyatām eti sarvādhiṣṭhātṛtaiva mādhyasthyam ity uktam

lines: As the Lord is compass-cleaver, so the sun —
for sire's own is wisdom's might, thus sung:
there, there, there the east is of the manifest from the east;
and just where, so there — thus self-ruled even, one's-own-place facing, in front.
tsa-a13-v23.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ yathā bhagavān digvibhāgakārī tathā sūryo 'pi sa hi pārameśvary eva jñānaśaktir ity uktaṃ tatra tatra tatra pūrvaṃ vyakteḥ pūrvā yatraiva ca tathā tatraiva evaṃ svātmādhīnāpi svasammukhīnasya deśasya purastāttvāt

lines: Thus by self, sun, Lord — the triad made one —
is the compass mused: so Abhinavagupta's masters.
Thus standing, facing northward sit, consuming body-hood
in frame, bulk, fire-pit and such, by non-ego-forgoing;
then near as strides another's frame, from disembodiedness —
through mounting the unwavering, blazing-seat, which comes ghost-like
to the point of the first vibration — this alone is form;
thereupon as taught is the worship-cakra of the gods;
chiefly here to be worshipped are the Shaktis.
tsa-a13-v25.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ sthite uttarābhimukham upaviśya dehapuryaṣṭakādau ahambhāvatyāgena dehatāṃ dahet saṃnidhāv api paradehavat adehatvāt tato nistaraṅgadhruvadhāmarūḍhasya dṛṣṭisvābhāvyāt yā kila ādyā spandakalā saiva mūrtiḥ tadupari yathopadiṣṭayājyadevatācakranyāsaḥ prādhānyena ca iha śaktayo yājyāḥ

lines: From being that seat, of the Lord-nine-fold self and such —
of energy alone sung well, so sages claim.
tsa-a13-v26.sanskrit_cite: tadāsanatvāt bhagavannavātmādīnāṃ śakter eva ca pūjyatvāt iti guravaḥ

lines: There the five states waking and the rest;
and sixth called the Unsurpassed, standing in native seat,
ever to be dwelt upon.
tsa-a13-v27.sanskrit_cite: tatra ca pañca avasthā jāgradādyāḥ ṣaṣṭhī ca anuttarā nāma svabhāvadaśā anusaṃdheyā

lines: Thus sixfold is the placing done.
There from the seat of our kings: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra — Lords, controlled;
for each from six-and-thirty-count nature-transcending bounds
in the Lord-blest irreversible mould full-ripe worship is: thus the Bhairavī-state —
the future often shines.
tsa-a13-v29.sanskrit_cite: tatra kāraṇānāṃ brahmaviṣṇurudreśasadāśivaśaktirūpāṇāṃ pratyekam adhiṣṭhānāt ṣaṭtriṃśattattvakalāpasya laukikatattvottīrṇasya bhairavabhaṭṭārakābhedavṛtte nyāse pūrṇatvāt bhairavībhāvaḥ tena etat anavakāśam

lines: Which, they cry: gained in waveless mounting,
what again with nature-forthbringing,
by placing and the rest — thus.
tsa-a13-v30.sanskrit_cite: yad āhuḥ ataraṅgarūḍhau labdhāyāṃ punaḥ kiṃ tattvasṛṣṭir nyāsādinā iti

lines: So far indeed that waveless Bhairava-formed,
which in own self shows forth-dissolve-variety's utmost.
tsa-a13-v31.sanskrit_cite: tāvat hi tad ataraṅgaṃ bhairavavapuḥ yat svātmani avabhāsitasṛṣṭisaṃhārāvaicitryakoṭi

lines: Thus all-pure mind-and-body made the Highest,
and outside, burnt offerings set in blossoms,
as possible each work and worship.
tsa-a13-v32.sanskrit_cite: evam anyonyamelakayogena parameśvarībhūtaṃ prāṇadehabuddhyādi bhāvayitvā bahir antaḥ puṣpadhūpatarpaṇādyair yathāsambhavaṃ pūjayet

lines: There in body, breath, mind moist, the thorned lotus for worship bring —
as at the root of power-substance seed, bulb, moons-pith,
in the east the flank is subtle; to the principle's end its crab;
the staff, the knot of Māyā, the square nature of pure cunning's lotus-bloom;
there stands the ever-lord Sadāśiva, he alone the great heat,
in pellucid grace to awaken the dawn;
pale with bitterest love, he stood on his threatening knee,
from the ground melting, consuming sounds,
and from a flimsy shore should wed the moon.
tsa-a13-v33.sanskrit_cite: tatra śarīre prāṇe dhiyi ca tadanusāreṇa śūlābjanyāsaṃ kuryāt tad yathā ādhāraśaktimūle mūlaṃ kanda āmūlasārakaṃ lambikānte kalātattvānto daṇḍaḥ māyātmako granthiḥ catuṣkikātmā śuddhavidyāpadmaṃ tatraiva sadāśivabhaṭṭārakaḥ sa eva mahāpretaḥ prakarṣeṇa līnatvāt bodhāt prādhānyena vedyātmakadehakṣayāt nādāmarśātmakatvāc ca iti

lines: That risen from the navel, venting through the triple crown-gate above,
dwelling within sound, a spreading power,
of even mind and form and the rest, the six-end;
thereon the pure tri-lotus, past the mind;
on this world-made division, made a seat,
presiding in pervading guise,
the wished-for, upheld being,
the goddess to be shaped —
which here, in self-sameness-full nature,
world-being-offered: that alone is worship;
which, the same, becoming-that: that is brooding;
which by such inward musing's steadfast poise: that is murmur;
which by such musing's order-wakened splendour's might:
by that force alone is all-world-selfing:
that is the burnt-gift;
that done, the train, from That
as sparks from a fire-heap,
musing thus, worship just so.
tsa-a13-v34.sanskrit_cite: tan nābhyutthitaṃ tanmūrdharandhratrayanirgataṃ nādāntarvartiśaktivyāpinīsamanārūpamarātrayaṃ dviṣaṭkāntaṃ tadupari śuddhapadmatrayam aunmanasam etasmin viśvamaye bhede āsanīkṛte adhiṣṭhātṛtayā vyāpakabhāvena ādheyabhūtāṃ yathābhimatāṃ devatāṃ kalpayitvā yat tatraiva samasvabhāvanirbharātmani viśvabhāvārpaṇaṃ tad eva pūjanaṃ yad eva tanmayībhavanaṃ tad dhyānaṃ yat tathāvidhāntaḥparāmarśasadbhāvanādāndolanaṃ sa japaḥ yat tathāvidhaparāmarśakramaprabuddhamahātejasā tathābalād eva viśvātmīkaraṇaṃ sa homaḥ tad evaṃ kṛtvā parivāraṃ tata eva vahnirāśer visphuliṅgavat dhyātvā tathaiva pūjayet

lines: Remembering the twelve-end, this foremost trident, from the root.
tsa-a13-v35.sanskrit_cite: dvādaśāntam idaṃ prāgraṃ viśūlaṃ mūlataḥ smaran

lines: Leaving sequence, going to goddess-wheel-front attains sky-going-ness.
From root-support, of twice-six-end-sky-peak-filling nature.
Of sky-going-ness, from sky-faring-rest and from sky-nectar-feasting.
Thus by inward rite alone, in sooth, is done what was to do.
Truly for the then-entered, still outer is to be done, to cut off the bound —
and who too thus shares not the sinking —
his chief is the outer rite;
from its doing, sinking's gain;
since for him too, but the beast-veiling inner rite,
when mounted thereon, of his thought-force is purity-giving.
tsa-a13-v40.sanskrit_cite: satyataḥ tadāviṣṭasya tathāpi bahir api kāryo yāgo 'vacchedahānaya eva yo 'pi tathā samāveśabhāk na bhavati tasya mukhyo bahiryāgaḥ tadabhyāsāt samāveśalābho yatas tasyāpi tu paśutātirodhānāyāntaryāgaḥ tadarūḍhāv api tatsaṃkalpabalasya śuddhipradatvāt

lines: Now, when initiation one fain would do — then for staying's sake:
ground-taking, Gaṇeśa-worship, jar-and-jug worship,
altar-worship, oblation — thus do.
tsa-a13-v41.sanskrit_cite: atha yadā dīkṣāṃ cikīrṣet tadādhivāsanārthaṃ bhūmiparigrahaṃ gaṇeśārcanaṃ kumbhakalaśayoḥ pūjāṃ sthaṇḍilārcanaṃ havanaṃ ca kuryāt

lines: But in daily-and-seasonal: altar-and-the-rest worship-oblation alone.
There is the staying, the pupil's cultured fitness-placing —
as the whetting of teeth; the God's toward-work-upturned-ness-grasping,
the master's taking of that.
tsa-a13-v43.sanskrit_cite: tatra adhivāsanaṃ śiṣyasya saṃskṛtayogyatādhānam amblīkaraṇam iva dantānāṃ devasya kartavyonmukhatvagrāhaṇam guros tadgrahaṇam

lines: Of rite-things, indoors abiding in the worship-house,
through the Lord's out-blooming glory,
bestowing worship-gear's fitness — thus.
There, the worship-house with all gear replete arranged,
having brought to mind the blest Mālinī or Mother,
full of her-letter-splendour's mass, bearing the taken,
musing, the flower-handful cast.
tsa-a13-v45.sanskrit_cite: tatra sarvopakaraṇapūrṇaṃ yāgagṛhaṃ vidhāya bhagavatīṃ mālinīṃ mātṛkāṃ vā smṛtvā tadvarṇatejaḥpuñjabharitaṃ gṛhītaṃ bhāvayan puṣpāñjaliṃ kṣipet

lines: Then the said weapon-muttered white grain and the rest, splendour-formed,
having strewn, in the north-east quarter gather in order —
thus the ground-taking.
tsa-a13-v46.sanskrit_cite: tata uktāstrajaptāni yathāsambhavaṃ siddhārthadhānyākṣatalājādīni tejorūpāṇi vikīrya aiśānyāṃ diśi krameṇa saṃghaṭṭayet iti bhūparigrahaḥ

lines: Then, the seat to pure-lore's term given, Gaṇeśa worshipped;
then the jar, with bliss-stuff filled, adorned, worshipped;
then the to-be-worshipped next, the betel placed,
there the chief spell, all-presiding, remembering, with rule before —
with that, a hundred-and-eight-muttered, that jar be made.
tsa-a13-v47.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ śuddhavidyāntam āsanaṃ dattvā gaṇapateḥ pūjā tataḥ kumbham ānandadravyapūritam alaṃkṛtaṃ pūjayet tato yājyam anu pūgaṃ nyasya tatra mukhyaṃ mantraṃ sarvādhiṣṭhātṛtayā vidhipūrvakatvena smaran aṣṭottaraśatamantritaṃ tena taṃ kumbhaṃ kuryāt

lines: In the twin jar, for stumbling-quelling, the weapon worship.
Then in own quarters the world-wards with weapons worship.
Then to the fore-hallowed pupil's hand the weapon-jar give.
tsa-a13-v50.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ śiṣyasya prāk dīkṣitasya haste astrakalaśaṃ dadyāt

lines: And himself the master the jar take up.
Then the pupil pouring the stream round the house for stumbling-quelling,
with jar let him follow, this spell reciting:
ho, ho! Indra! by thee in thine own quarter, for stumbling-pacifying.
tsa-a13-v52.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ śiṣyaṃ gṛhaparyanteṣu vighnaśamanāya dhārāṃ pātayantaṃ sakumbho 'nugacchet imaṃ mantraṃ paṭhan bho bhoḥ śakra tvayā svasyāṃ diśi vighnapraśāntaye

lines: With heedfulness, to rite's end must it be, by Śiva's behest.
In the three-syllabled name, 'ho' is one alone — thus.
tsa-a13-v54.sanskrit_cite: tryakṣare nāmni bho ity ekam eva

lines: Then in the north-east quarter the jar establish.
Upon the strewn, the weapon-jar.
Then worship of the twain.
Then in the altar's midst the Highest's worship.
Then the fire-pit as Highest-Might-formed mused, the fire kindled there,
with heart-inward waking-fire made one,
with spell-musing's train, the blazing Śiva-fire mused,
there placed, worshipped, the spells with ghee and grain to sate.
tsa-a13-v59.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ agnikuṇḍaṃ parameśvaraśaktirūpatayā bhāvayitvā tatra agniṃ prajvālya hṛdayāntarbodhāgninā saha ekīkṛtya mantraparāmarśasāhityena jvalantaṃ śivāgniṃ bhāvayitvā tatra nyasya abhyarcya mantrān tarpayet ājyena tilaiś ca

lines: And with the bowl, the sprinkling alone is grain-and-ghee's refining.
tsa-a13-v60.sanskrit_cite: arghapātreṇa ca prokṣaṇam eva tilājyādīnāṃ saṃskāraḥ

lines: And of ladle-and-spoon, no-difference-view alone indeed is refining.
tsa-a13-v61.sanskrit_cite: sruksruvayoś ca parameśābhedadṛṣṭir eva hi saṃskāraḥ

lines: Then offered as may be, the ladle-spoon up-down-faced, as might-and-Śiva formed,
mutually facing, arranged, even-footed risen,
musing the stream of supreme nectar fallen, risen in the sky of the twelve-end, risen full-Śiva-moon,
and breathing the vauṣaḍ-ending spell, till ghee's end stand —
thus the full-pouring, spell-wheel-sating.
tsa-a13-v62.sanskrit_cite: tato yathāśakti hutvā sruksruvau ūrdhvādhomukhatayā śaktiśivarūpau parasparonmukhau vidhāya samapādotthito dvādaśāntagaganoditaśivapūrṇacandraniḥsṛtapatatparāmṛtadhārābhāvanāṃ kurvan vauṣaḍantaṃ mantram uccārayan ca ājyakṣayāntaṃ tiṣṭhet iti pūrṇāhutiḥ mantracakrasaṃtarpaṇī

lines: Then the sprinkled grain brought, on hearth-vessel-jar-fires share by share offered,
one share left over, to the pupil a share give.
tsa-a13-v63.sanskrit_cite: tataś caruṃ prokṣitam ānīya sthaṇḍilakalaśakumbhavahniṣu bhāgaṃ bhāgaṃ nivedya ekabhāgam avaśeṣya śiṣyāya bhāgaṃ dadyāt

lines: Then the tooth-twig.
Its fall in fire-Yama-Nirṛti directions and below is ill — thus.
tsa-a13-v65.sanskrit_cite: tatpāto 'gniyamanirṛtidikṣu adhaś ca na śubha iti

lines: There by weapon-spell the burnt-gift be done.
Then the stumbling shunned, to see the coming spell made worthy,
bring the blindfold pupil in, make him kneel,
cast thou the blossom-handful.
tsa-a13-v67.sanskrit_cite: tato vikṣepaparihāreṇa bhāvimantradarśanayogyatāyai baddhanetraṃ śiṣyaṃ praveśya jānusthitaṃ taṃ kṛtvā puṣpāñjaliṃ kṣepayet

lines: Then swift, eye-cloth loosed of him — through grace-descent blessed means —
seeing face to face the present spell of that station, made of that he becomes;
of graced means the spell-presence is plain,
since as if trembling, the beings.
tsa-a13-v68.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ sahasā apāsitanetrabandho 'sau śaktipātānugṛhītakaraṇatvāt saṃnihitamantraṃ tatsthānaṃ sākṣātkāreṇa paśyan tanmayo bhavati anugṛhītakaraṇānāṃ mantrasaṃnidhiḥ pratyakṣaḥ yatas trasyatām iva bhūtānām

lines: Then in one's own right hand, blazing, the god-wheel worshipped,
that hand burning the pupil's bonds on crown-heart-navel, lay down.
tsa-a13-v69.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ svadakṣiṇahaste dīpyatayā devatācakraṃ pūjayitvā taṃ hastaṃ mūrdhahṛnnābhiṣu śiṣyasya pāśān dahantaṃ nikṣipet

lines: Then in the left with gentleness, worshipped, fattened with pure truth —
then make obeisance.
tsa-a13-v70.sanskrit_cite: tato vāme somyatayā pūjayitvā śuddhatattvāpyāyinaṃ tataḥ praṇāmaṃ kuryāt

lines: Then the being-god-quarter-bali, with wine-flesh-ghee full,
without bestow — sip thou.
tsa-a13-v71.sanskrit_cite: tato bhūtadevatādigbaliṃ madyamāṃsajalādipūrṇaṃ bahir dadyāt ācāmeta

lines: Then, thyself the grain-feast done, with pupil-self oneness won,
awakened-natured, stay.
tsa-a13-v72.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ svayaṃ carubhojanaṃ kṛtvā śiṣyātmanā saha aikyam āpannaḥ prabuddhavṛttiḥ tiṣṭhet

lines: Dreaming too, at dawn if the pupil an ill dream tell,
that to him expound thou not.
tsa-a13-v73.sanskrit_cite: svapan api prabhāte śiṣyaḥ cet aśubhaṃ svapnaṃ vadet tat asmai na vyākuryāt

lines: For doubt-and-fear would his be; with weapon alone its cleansing do.
tsa-a13-v74.sanskrit_cite: śaṅkātaṅkau hi tathāsya syātām kevalam astreṇa tanniṣkṛtiṃ kuryāt

lines: Then just so the Highest worshipped, into him by the pupil's breath-course entered,
touching the six-fold six in heart-throat-palate-brow-cleft-twelve's-end,
each eight refinings musing, somewhile the pupil's breath there resting,
again descend.
tsa-a13-v75.sanskrit_cite: tatas tathaiva parameśvaraṃ pūjayitvā tadagre śiṣyasya prāṇakrameṇa praviśya hṛtkaṇṭhatālulalāṭarandhradvādaśānteṣu ṣaṭsu kāraṇaṣaṭkasparśaṃ kurvan pratyekam aṣṭau saṃskārān cintayan kaṃcit kālaṃ śiṣyaprāṇaṃ tatraiva viśramayya punar avarohet

lines: Thus effected-eight-and-forty refinings, made Rudra's part:
a time-bound one becomes.
Then to him the worship-to-be spell with blossoms and the rest bestow.
tsa-a13-v77.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ asmai pūjyaṃ mantraṃ puṣpādyaiḥ saha arpayet

lines: Then the vows to him set forth.
In master whole-souled, love; so in writ; in God; from their foes aversion;
as to the master, to master's son and the rest;
of lore-bound wrought, of fore-hallowed and the rest, beholding;
of womb-tie, for its honouring, not of self — thus deem.
tsa-a13-v79.sanskrit_cite: gurau sarvātmanā bhaktiḥ tathā śāstre deve tatpratidvaṃdvini parāṅmukhatā guruvat guruputrādeḥ vidyāsambandhakṛtasya tatpūrvadīkṣitādeḥ saṃdarśanam yaunasambandhasya tadārādhanārtham na tu svata iti mantavyam

lines: Woman's — of the barren a loathing-cause make thou not.
God-name, master-name, and spell, save at worship's hour, breathe thou not.
tsa-a13-v81.sanskrit_cite: devatānāma gurunāma tathā mantraṃ pūjākālāt ṛte na uccārayet

lines: What the master has enjoyed — couch and the rest — enjoy thou not.
What games and the rest are worldly, that, the master by, do thou not.
tsa-a13-v83.sanskrit_cite: yat kiṃcit laukikaṃ krīḍādi tat gurusaṃnidhau na kuryāt

lines: Save by that, elsewhere excellence-fancy make thou not.
Everywhere, at sire-rites and the rest, the master alone worship.
And in all occasionals, she-goblin and the rest — utter no names.
tsa-a13-v86.sanskrit_cite: sarveṣu ca naimittikeṣu śākinītyādiśabdān na vadet

lines: Feast-days worship keep.
With the down-looking Vaiṣṇavas and the rest, company keep thou not.
tsa-a13-v88.sanskrit_cite: vaiṣṇavādyair adhodṛṣṭibhiḥ saha saṃgatiṃ na kuryāt

lines: Abiding in this writ, with former-birth conceit, regard thou not.
When the master's circle to thy house has come, as thou canst, worship do.
The downward-pathed, though Vaiṣṇavite and the rest,
having e'en made him thy master, from his writ-clan cast away.
tsa-a13-v91.sanskrit_cite: adhomārgasthitaṃ kaṃcit vaiṣṇavādyaṃ tacchāstrakulāt gurūkṛtyāpi tyajet

lines: Even then with excellence-fancy regard him not.
With lingam-bearers make no mingling rite;
them only as thou canst, worship.
tsa-a13-v93.sanskrit_cite: liṅgibhiḥ saha samācāramelanaṃ na kuryāt tān kevalaṃ yathāśakti pūjayet

lines: Doubts abandon thou.
In the wheel abiding, last-and-first sundering, birth-wrought, fancy thou not.
tsa-a13-v95.sanskrit_cite: cakre sthitaś caramāgryādivibhāgaṃ janmakṛtaṃ na saṃkalpayet

lines: Apart from frame, no other seat or ford and the rest with high honour regard.
tsa-a13-v96.sanskrit_cite: śarīrāt ṛte na anyat āyatanatīrthādikaṃ bahumānena paśyet

lines: Mantra-heart unceasing mind thou — thus the pupil, hearing, bowing,
owning, to the master, with fee to wife-and-wealth-and-frame,
well-pleasing, sating fore-hallowed and needy-fatherless.
tsa-a13-v97.sanskrit_cite: mantrahṛdayam anavarataṃ smaret ity evaṃ śiṣyaḥ śrutvā praṇamya abhyupagamya guruṃ dhanadāraśarīraparyantayā dakṣiṇayā paritoṣya pūrvadīkṣitāṃś ca dīnānāthādikān tarpayet

lines: And by the future rule the image-wheel sate thou.
So is the timeling made.
In spell-practice, daily worship, hearing, study — entitled;
but in the occasional, everywhere, the master alone beseech.
tsa-a13-v100.sanskrit_cite: mantrābhyāse nityapūjāyāṃ śravaṇe 'dhyayane adhikārī naimittike tu sarvatra gurum eva abhyarthayet

lines: Thus is the timeling's rule.

tsa-a13-v31.note: Parser-reconstructed tokens; consult the edition for exact typography.
